Edge weights are values used in the connections between nodes in a neural network, and in the context of the paper, they are discussed in relation to the computational power of RNNs and GRUs. The paper mentions that allowing infinite edge weights and nonlinear output activation functions makes GRUs at least as computationally powerful as pushdown automata.

The sentences in WikiGenderBias are curated by using a variant of the Distant Supervision assumption, where for a given relation between two entities, any sentence from an article written about one of those entities that mentions the other entity is assumed to express the relation. Additionally, the dataset is generated by collecting sentences from Wikipedia articles about entities, and the gender information for entities is obtained from Wikipedia. Ground truth labels are obtained by annotating sentences with AMT workers.

The editors' annotations in KPTimes differ from those in existing datasets in that they are more uniform and consistent, with editors using a controlled indexing vocabulary and being more likely to generalize and assign keyphrases that do not occur in the document.

The training objective in the method introduced in this paper is to reduce catastrophic forgetting during domain adaptation for reading comprehension by incorporating auxiliary penalty terms to the standard cross entropy loss to regularise the fine-tuning process.

The improvement in performance brought by lexicon pruning on a simple EM algorithm is that it reduces search error during training, resulting in models with lower Morfessor costs. Lower costs also lead to improved accuracy when segmentation output is compared to linguistic morphological segmentation.
The Global encoder and Slot-Attentive decoders (G-SAT) architecture provides the most speedup.

They generate input noise for the encoder and decoder by simulating three typical operations: 1) random dropping: randomly dropping the input tokens of encoder and decoder respectively with different drop rates; 2) random noising: randomly selecting tokens and replacing its embedding with random noise; 3) random swapping: randomly reversing the order for the adjacent tokens.
The sentiment features used are the sentiment lexicon features generated using the Hu and Liu Lexicon, Norms of Valence, Arousal, and Dominance, labMT, and NRC Emoticon Lexicon.

The speakers' reputations bias the dataset by influencing the ratings given to their talks. This bias is addressed by confining the analysis to the transcripts only and normalizing the ratings to remove the effects of unwanted variables such as the speakers' reputations, publicity, and contemporary hot topics.

limitations: Official token-overlap metric on 40 selected source questions, not full QASPER test; known-paper prompts and code-execution conditions differ from published full-test systems.

All original reference annotations are scored and the maximum answer F1 is used. Literal submitted strings receive only official SQuAD-style normalization; no protocol abstention paraphrase is rewritten to Unanswerable.

No-submission, error, escalated, or unrecorded episodes are missing predictions: zero in the 40-question overall mean. Empty submitted strings also score zero. Official answer-type means omit missing predictions and choose the first maximizing reference.
No Evidence F1 is reported: character spans were not converted to QASPER paragraphs. Answer F1 is not semantic support review or a validated model-improvement gate.
